docs.title: Request Routing Logic
docs.text:
FactoryLM intelligently routes each request to the most appropriate layer:

def route_query(query, context):
    # LAYER 0: Knowledge base first (instant, free)
    kb_result = knowledge_base.search(query)
    if kb_result.confidence > 0.9:
        return kb_result

    # LAYER 0: Check for matching workflow
    workflow = plane.match_workflow(query)
    if workflow:
        return workflow.execute()

    # LAYER 1: Edge LLM for simple commands
    if is_simple_command(query):
        return edge_llm.process(query)

    # LAYER 2: Local GPU for medium complexity
    if gpu_server.available:
        return gpu_server.process(query)

    # LAYER 3: Cloud as last resort
    if cloud.available and not air_gapped:
        return cloud.process(query)

docs.title: Read-Only Safety Principle
docs.text:
A fundamental architectural principle of FactoryLM is the read-only constraint:

What FactoryLM Does

  • ✅ Read tag values from PLCs and industrial systems
  • ✅ Monitor I/O states in real-time
  • ✅ Record fault codes and maintenance history
  • ✅ Analyze trends and predict issues
  • ✅ Suggest actions based on expert knowledge

What FactoryLM Never Does

  • ❌ Write to PLCs - Read-only for safety
  • ❌ Change setpoints - Diagnostic tool only
  • ❌ Start/stop equipment - No control functions
  • ❌ Modify programs - Observation only

This constraint eliminates fear, simplifies IT approval, and removes liability while providing maximum diagnostic value.

# Complex pattern matching
def match_query_pattern(query):
    # Normalize query
    normalized = query.lower().strip()

    # Check for exact matches first
    if normalized in known_responses:
        return known_responses[normalized]

    # Pattern matching
    for pattern, handler in patterns.items():
        if re.match(pattern, normalized):
            return execute_handler(handler, query)

    # No match - escalate to Layer 1
    return None

def process_query(query, context):
    # First check Layer 0
    layer0_response = knowledge_base.search(query)
    if layer0_response.confidence > 0.9:
        return layer0_response

    # Process with Layer 1
    complexity_score = assess_query_complexity(query)

    if complexity_score < 0.7:
        # Handle with Layer 1
        response = edge_llm.process(query, context)

        # Learn from successful responses
        if response.success:
            knowledge_base.add_pattern(query, response)

        return response
    else:
        # Escalate to Layer 2 or 3
        return escalate_query(query, context)

Here's how the different components work together to process a typical user query:

docs.title: Discovery Engine
docs.text:
class IndustrialDiscovery:
    INDUSTRIAL_PORTS = {
        502: 'Modbus TCP',
        44818: 'EtherNet/IP', 
        4840: 'OPC-UA',
        102: 'S7 Communication',
        2404: 'IEC 61850',
        20000: 'DNP3'
    }

    async def discover_network(self):
        devices = []

        # mDNS discovery
        mdns_devices = await self.mdns_scan()
        devices.extend(mdns_devices)

        # Port scanning
        ip_range = self.get_network_range()
        for ip in ip_range:
            for port, protocol in self.INDUSTRIAL_PORTS.items():
                if await self.port_open(ip, port):
                    device = await self.fingerprint_device(ip, port, protocol)
                    devices.append(device)

        return devices

docs.title: Getting Started with FactoryLM
docs.text: Welcome to FactoryLM! This section will help you get up and running quickly with the industrial AI platform.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: FactoryLM is designed to be deployed in various configurations depending on your security requirements, infrastructure, and budget. Whether you're running a full stack with cloud connectivity or an air-gapped deployment for maximum security, we have you covered.

docs.title: Deployment Scenarios
docs.text: Choose the deployment scenario that best fits your needs:

docs.title: A: Full Stack (Internet Available)
docs.text:
All layers available. Maximum intelligence.

  • Layer 0: Code + Knowledge Base (Raspberry Pi)
  • Layer 1: Edge LLM (Raspberry Pi)
  • Layer 2: Local GPU Server (air-gapped)
  • Layer 3: Cloud AI (Claude, GPT-4, etc.)

Best for: General industrial environments with internet access

docs.title: B: Air-Gapped (Defense/ITAR)
docs.text:
Layer 3 disabled. 70B local model. Data never leaves facility.

  • Layer 0: Code + Knowledge Base (Raspberry Pi)
  • Layer 1: Edge LLM (Raspberry Pi)
  • Layer 2: Local GPU Server (air-gapped)
  • Layer 3: ❌ Disabled

Best for: Defense contractors, ITAR-controlled environments, high-security facilities

docs.title: C: Budget (No GPU Server)
docs.text:
Skip Layer 2. Pi + Cloud only.

  • Layer 0: Code + Knowledge Base (Raspberry Pi)
  • Layer 1: Edge LLM (Raspberry Pi)
  • Layer 2: ❌ Skipped
  • Layer 3: Cloud AI (Claude, GPT-4, etc.)

Best for: Small facilities, proof-of-concept deployments, budget-conscious implementations

docs.title: D: Maximum Security (Pi Only)
docs.text:
Layer 0 only. Completely isolated.

  • Layer 0: Code + Knowledge Base (Raspberry Pi)
  • Layer 1: ❌ Disabled
  • Layer 2: ❌ Disabled
  • Layer 3: ❌ Disabled

Best for: Maximum security environments, completely air-gapped facilities

FactoryLM is a read-only diagnostic tool. It never writes to PLCs or controls equipment. However, always follow your facility's safety procedures when connecting any device to industrial networks.

Network Security

Consider network segmentation and firewall rules when deploying FactoryLM. While it only reads data, it's good practice to isolate industrial networks from corporate networks.

docs.title: Your First Project
docs.text: This guide will walk you through setting up your first FactoryLM project, connecting to industrial equipment, and performing basic operations.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
In this tutorial, you'll:

  1. Create a new FactoryLM project
  2. Connect to a PLC (Allen-Bradley MicroLogix example)
  3. Configure tag monitoring
  4. Set up alerts and notifications
  5. Test the voice interface
  6. Explore the web dashboard

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have:

  • FactoryLM installed and running (Installation Guide)
  • Network access to your industrial equipment
  • Equipment documentation (IP address, protocol details)
  • Mobile device with WhatsApp or Telegram

docs.title: Step 1: Create a New Project
docs.text:
Projects in FactoryLM organize your equipment, tags, and configurations:

# Create a new project
factorylm project create "Production Line A" \
  --description "Main production line monitoring" \
  --location "Building 1, Floor 2"

# Switch to the new project
factorylm project use "Production Line A"

You can also create projects via the web interface at http://<pi-ip>:8080/projects.

docs.title: Step 2: Add Your First Device
docs.text: Let's connect to an Allen-Bradley MicroLogix PLC as our example:

docs.title: Discover Devices
docs.text:
First, scan your network for available devices:

# Scan for EtherNet/IP devices
factorylm scan ethernet-ip --network 192.168.1.0/24

# Scan for Modbus devices
factorylm scan modbus --network 192.168.1.0/24 --ports 502

# Scan for OPC UA servers
factorylm scan opcua --network 192.168.1.0/24

docs.title: Add the Device
docs.text:
Based on your scan results, add the device:

EtherNet/IP (Allen-Bradley)Modbus TCPOPC UA 
factorylm device add \
  --name "Main PLC" \
  --type "MicroLogix 1400" \
  --protocol ethernet-ip \
  --ip 192.168.1.100 \
  --slot 0 \
  --description "Primary production control PLC"

factorylm device add \
  --name "Main PLC" \
  --type "Generic PLC" \
  --protocol modbus-tcp \
  --ip 192.168.1.100 \
  --port 502 \
  --unit-id 1 \
  --description "Primary production control PLC"

factorylm device add \
  --name "SCADA Server" \
  --type "OPC UA Server" \
  --protocol opcua \
  --endpoint "opc.tcp://192.168.1.100:4840" \
  --security-mode none \
  --description "Main SCADA OPC UA server"

docs.title: Verify Connection
docs.text:
Test the connection to ensure everything is working:

# Test device connection
factorylm device test "Main PLC"

# View device information
factorylm device info "Main PLC"

Expected output: 

✅ Connection successful
📊 Device Type: MicroLogix 1400
🌐 IP Address: 192.168.1.100
🔧 Protocol: EtherNet/IP
⚡ Status: Online
📈 Response Time: 23ms

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Tag Monitoring
docs.text: Tags represent data points you want to monitor (temperature, pressure, motor status, etc.):

docs.title: Auto-Discovery
docs.text:
Let FactoryLM automatically discover available tags:

# Discover all available tags
factorylm tags discover "Main PLC"

# Show discovered tags
factorylm tags list "Main PLC"

docs.title: Manual Tag Configuration
docs.text:
Add specific tags you want to monitor:

# Add analog input (temperature)
factorylm tag add \
  --device "Main PLC" \
  --name "Tank_Temperature" \
  --address "N7:0" \
  --type "INT" \
  --unit "°C" \
  --description "Main tank temperature"

# Add digital input (motor status)
factorylm tag add \
  --device "Main PLC" \
  --name "Conveyor_Motor" \
  --address "I:0/0" \
  --type "BOOL" \
  --description "Conveyor motor running status"

# Add analog output (pressure setpoint)
factorylm tag add \
  --device "Main PLC" \
  --name "Pressure_Setpoint" \
  --address "F8:0" \
  --type "REAL" \
  --unit "PSI" \
  --description "System pressure setpoint"

docs.title: Tag Groups
docs.text:
Organize related tags into groups:

# Create tag groups
factorylm tag-group create "Temperature Sensors" \
  --tags "Tank_Temperature,Ambient_Temperature,Motor_Temperature"

factorylm tag-group create "Motor Status" \
  --tags "Conveyor_Motor,Pump_Motor,Fan_Motor"

docs.title: Step 4: Set Up Alerts and Notifications
docs.text: Configure alerts to be notified when values go outside normal ranges:

docs.title: Temperature Alert
docs.text:
factorylm alert create \
  --name "High Tank Temperature" \
  --tag "Tank_Temperature" \
  --condition "value > 80" \
  --priority "high" \
  --message "Tank temperature is {{value}}°C - exceeds 80°C limit" \
  --channels "whatsapp,telegram"

docs.title: Motor Status Alert
docs.text:
factorylm alert create \
  --name "Conveyor Motor Stopped" \
  --tag "Conveyor_Motor" \
  --condition "value == false" \
  --priority "medium" \
  --message "Conveyor motor has stopped unexpectedly" \
  --channels "telegram"

docs.title: Multi-Condition Alert
docs.text:
factorylm alert create \
  --name "System Health Check" \
  --condition "(Tank_Temperature > 85) OR (Conveyor_Motor == false AND Production_Mode == true)" \
  --priority "critical" \
  --message "Critical system issue detected - immediate attention required" \
  --channels "whatsapp,telegram,email"

docs.title: Step 5: Test Communication
docs.text: Now let's test the communication interfaces:

docs.title: WhatsApp/Telegram Testing
docs.text: Send these messages to your FactoryLM bot:

docs.title: Basic Queries
docs.text:
What's the status of Main PLC?

Show me the current tank temperature

Is the conveyor motor running?

docs.title: Advanced Queries
docs.text:
What's the trend for tank temperature over the last hour?

Are there any alarms on Main PLC?

Show me all motor statuses

docs.title: Voice Interface Testing
docs.text:
If you have voice enabled (Halo glasses or phone):

  1. Call your FactoryLM phone number
  2. Say: "Status of main PLC"
  3. Listen for the response
  4. Try: "What's the tank temperature?"

docs.title: Expected Responses
docs.text:
The system should respond with current values:

Tank Temperature: 72.5°C Conveyor Motor: Running ✅ System Status: Normal Last Update: 2 seconds ago

docs.title: Step 6: Explore the Web Dashboard
docs.text: Open your web browser and navigate to http://<pi-ip>:8080:

docs.title: Dashboard Overview
docs.text:
The main dashboard shows:

  • Real-time tag values with color-coded status
  • Device health and connection status
  • Active alerts and recent events
  • System performance metrics

docs.title: Key Features to Explore
docs.text:
1. Live Data View: Real-time updates every few seconds
  2. Historical Trends: Click any tag to see historical data
  3. Alert Management: View, acknowledge, and configure alerts
  4. Device Configuration: Add/edit devices and tags
  5. System Health: Monitor FactoryLM performance

docs.title: Creating Custom Views
docs.text:
Create a custom dashboard for your production line:

  1. Click "Create Dashboard"
  2. Add widgets for your key metrics:
  3. Tank Temperature (Gauge)
  4. Motor Status (LED Indicators)
  5. Pressure Trends (Line Chart)
  6. Alert Summary (Table)
  7. Save as "Production Line A Overview"

docs.title: Step 7: Knowledge Base Integration
docs.text: FactoryLM learns from your interactions. Let's seed it with some knowledge:

docs.title: Upload Equipment Documentation
docs.text:
# Upload PLC manual
factorylm knowledge upload \
  --file "MicroLogix_1400_Manual.pdf" \
  --type "equipment-manual" \
  --device "Main PLC"

# Upload troubleshooting guide
factorylm knowledge upload \
  --file "Troubleshooting_Guide.pdf" \
  --type "troubleshooting" \
  --tags "Tank_Temperature,Conveyor_Motor"

docs.title: Test Knowledge Integration
docs.text:
Ask questions that require the uploaded documentation:

What should I do if the tank temperature exceeds 85°C?

How do I reset fault code F01 on the MicroLogix?

docs.title: Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Ensure everything is working correctly:

  • Device shows as "Connected" in status
  • Can read all configured tag values
  • Alerts trigger when conditions are met
  • WhatsApp/Telegram responds to queries
  • Web dashboard displays real-time data
  • Voice interface responds (if enabled)
  • Knowledge base answers equipment questions

docs.title: Device Won't Connect
docs.text:
Check network connectivity: 

ping 192.168.1.100
nmap -p 502 192.168.1.100

Verify PLC settings: - EtherNet/IP: Ensure IP address and slot are correct - Modbus: Check unit ID and register addresses - OPC UA: Verify endpoint URL and security settings

docs.title: Installation Methods

docs.title: Method 1: Pre-built Image (Recommended)
docs.text:
The fastest way to get started is with our pre-built Raspberry Pi image:

  1. Download the latest image: 

    wget https://github.com/Mikecranesync/factorylm/releases/latest/download/factorylm-pi-image.zip

  2. Flash to SD card: 

    # Using Raspberry Pi Imager (Recommended)
rpi-imager

# Or using dd command (Linux/macOS)
unzip -p factorylm-pi-image.zip | sudo dd of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress

  3. First boot configuration: 

    # SSH into the Pi (default: pi/factorylm)
ssh pi@<pi-ip-address>

# Run setup wizard
sudo factorylm-config

docs.title: Method 2: Docker Installation
docs.text:
For x86_64 systems or when you want containerized deployment:

  1. Install Docker and Docker Compose: 

    # Ubuntu/Debian
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh
sudo sh get-docker.sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

# Install Docker Compose
sudo apt install docker-compose-plugin

  2. Deploy FactoryLM: 

    git clone https://github.com/Mikecranesync/factorylm.git
cd factorylm
docker compose up -d

  3. Configure via web interface: Open http://<server-ip>:8080 and follow the setup wizard.

docs.title: Method 3: Manual Installation
docs.text:
For custom environments or development:

  1. Install prerequisites: 

    # Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y \
  python3.10 python3-pip python3-venv \
  git curl build-essential \
  libmodbus-dev libssl-dev

# RHEL/CentOS
sudo dnf install -y \
  python3.10 python3-pip \
  git curl gcc openssl-devel \
  libmodbus-devel

  2. Clone and install: 

    git clone https://github.com/Mikecranesync/factorylm.git
cd factorylm
./scripts/install.sh

  3. Configure environment: 

    sudo systemctl enable factorylm
sudo systemctl start factorylm
factorylm-config

docs.title: Environment Configuration
docs.text: After installation, configure your environment:

docs.title: Core Settings
docs.text:
Create and edit the main configuration file:

sudo nano /etc/factorylm/config.yml

# FactoryLM Configuration
version: "0.25"

# Deployment scenario (full-stack, air-gapped, budget, security)
deployment: "full-stack"

# Layer configuration
layers:
  layer_0:
    enabled: true
    vector_db: "chroma"
    workflow_engine: true

  layer_1:
    enabled: true
    model: "qwen-0.5b"
    max_memory: "2GB"

  layer_2:
    enabled: false  # Set to true if you have GPU server
    model: "llama-70b"
    gpu_server: "192.168.1.100"

  layer_3:
    enabled: true
    provider: "groq"  # or "claude", "openai"
    api_key: "${GROQ_API_KEY}"

# Industrial protocols
protocols:
  modbus:
    enabled: true
    timeout: 5000

  ethernet_ip:
    enabled: true
    timeout: 5000

  opcua:
    enabled: true
    security_mode: "none"  # or "basic", "signandencrypt"

# User interfaces
interfaces:
  whatsapp:
    enabled: false  # Configure with WhatsApp Business API
    webhook_url: ""
    verify_token: ""

  telegram:
    enabled: true
    bot_token: "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}"

  web:
    enabled: true
    port: 8080
    ssl: false

# Logging and monitoring
logging:
  level: "INFO"
  file: "/var/log/factorylm/factorylm.log"
  max_size: "100MB"
  backup_count: 10

monitoring:
  enabled: true
  metrics_port: 9090
  health_check_interval: 30

docs.text:
# Abstract base class that ALL LLM clients must implement
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

class LLMResponse:
    """Standardized response object from any LLM"""
    def __init__(self, text: str, tokens_used: int, model: str):
        self.text = text
        self.tokens_used = tokens_used
        self.model = model

class BaseLLMClient(ABC):
    """Abstract interface for all LLM providers"""

    @abstractmethod
    def __init__(self, api_key: str, model: str):
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def analyze_machine_state(self, question: str, machine_state: Dict) -> LLMResponse:
        """Analyze PLC state and answer technician question"""
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def get_model_name(self) -> str:
        """Return the model name being used"""
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def estimate_cost(self, response: LLMResponse) -> float:
        """Estimate cost of this API call"""
        pass

Requirements: - [ ] All methods documented with docstrings - [ ] Type hints on all parameters - [ ] Standardized response format (LLMResponse) - [ ] Error handling interface defined

This is the core orchestrator that ties STT + LLM + TTS together.

class VoiceAgent:
    def __init__(self, llm_provider: str, stt_provider: str, tts_provider: str):
        self.llm = create_llm_client(llm_provider, ...)
        self.stt = create_stt_client(stt_provider)
        self.tts = create_tts_client(tts_provider)

    def run_loop(self):
        """Main voice interaction loop"""
        while True:
            # 1. Listen for question
            stt_result = self.stt.listen_for_question()
            if not stt_result:
                self.tts.speak("Sorry, I didn't hear that. Try again.")
                continue

            # 2. Check for exit command
            if "exit" in stt_result.text.lower():
                self.tts.speak("Goodbye!")
                break

            # 3. Read current machine state (from PRD-003)
            machine_state = self.plc_client.read_state()

            # 4. Call LLM to analyze
            llm_response = self.llm.analyze_machine_state(
                stt_result.text, 
                machine_state
            )

            # 5. Speak the answer
            self.tts.speak(llm_response.text)

def create_plc_client(plc_type: str, host: str, port: int = 502) -> BasePLCClient:
    """
    Factory function for PLC clients

    plc_types:
    - "factoryio_micro820" - Factory I/O + Micro 820 combo
    - "micro820" - Generic Micro 820 (use PRD-003)
    - "mock" - Mock PLC for testing
    """
    if plc_type == "factoryio_micro820":
        return FactoryIOMicro820(host, port)
    elif plc_type == "micro820":
        return Micro820PLC(host, port)
    elif plc_type == "mock":
        return MockPLC()
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown PLC type: {plc_type}")
